senses.definition_en: the practice of using le as a direct object pronoun when referring to people

examples.english: The phenomenon that we call leísmo consists of using the typical indirect object pronouns (le, les), which only reflect the number of the noun it replaces, in place of the proper direct object pronouns, which reflect number and gender (lo, los, la, las).
examples.ref: 2004, Serafina García García, Antonio J. Meilán García, Hortensia Martínez, Hortensia Martínez García, Construir bien en español: la forma de las palabras, Universidad de Oviedo, →ISBN, page 167:
examples.text: Se denomina leísmo al fenómeno que consiste en utilizar los pronombres típicos de complemento indirecto (le, les), que solo reflejan el número del sustantivo al que sustituyen, en lugar de los propios del complemento directo, que reflejan el número y el género (lo, los, la, las).
examples.translation: The phenomenon that we call leísmo consists of using the typical indirect object pronouns (le, les), which only reflect the number of the noun it replaces, in place of the proper direct object pronouns, which reflect number and gender (lo, los, la, las).

glosses: the practice of using le as a direct object pronoun when referring to people
